claims.claim: Hong Kong should tighten SDU rent control with a published per-square-foot rent band on initial rents rather than a hard cap.
A hard cap would help incumbents while shrinking the stock that houses the people the policy claims to protect.
The 2021 Tenancy Control Ordinance capped increases within existing tenancies but left initial rents untouched.
Median SDU rent per square foot rose 6.8 percent in 2019–2021 and still 3.1 percent under the ordinance, outpacing general private rent growth.
Real rent burden worsened from 31 to 34 percent.
Because the ordinance is non-binding at the point that matters, visible stock stability proves little.
First-generation rent controls (caps on levels) consistently cause stock contraction, while second-generation controls (caps on increases) have small or null effects.
The elasticity estimate for marginal stock is 0.31 to 0.48, so a 10 percent cap-induced reduction removes roughly 3 to 5 percent of stock over five years.
A modelled 15 percent cut in initial rents would transfer about 900 dollars a month to incumbents while leaving 3,000 to 4,000 households a year unable to enter the segment.
Berlin shows listings contracted within a year as owners withheld or rerouted flats, and suppressed increases released above the pre-cap trend when the law fell.
A hard cap framed as deprivation of income stream invites compensation claims and judicial review, while a published indexed band can be defended as rate-capping rather than confiscation.
New York's second-generation scheme shows modest stock contraction because first-rent regulation is light.
Inspection capacity covers under 6 percent of stock per year, and a band-based cap requires a certifiable tenancy register costing 40 to 60 staff-years.
Tenants least able to complain—those with no written agreement and the newest arrivals—would be missed first by enforcement.
The subcommittee could not identify any design protecting the newest-arrival tail first rather than last.
Rent is not the binding constraint tenants name; Mr Chan would accept any rent for a shorter waiting list.
The NGO survey finds 61 percent would trade a nominal increase for three-year tenure security and 74 percent for a faster public-housing offer.
Tenure security is cheap to enforce relative to a rent band and addresses the insecurity tenants call the worst part.

The recommendation is to enact a light indexed initial-rent band, fund the tenancy register first, pair it with statutory tenure security, and treat the public-housing queue as the real supply instrument.
A hard cap would buy incumbents 800 dollars a month and charge it to households still outside the door.

cites.sentence: The 2021 Tenancy Control Ordinance capped increases within an existing tenancy but left the initial rent untouched [D1p3], and that is precisely where the pain sits.
Mrs Wong, nine years in her unit with no written agreement, says the ordinance "changed nothing she can see" [D4p1].
The data agree: median SDU rent per square foot rose 6.8 percent in 2019–2021, then still 3.1 percent under the ordinance, against general private rent growth of 2.4 and 1.7 percent [D2p2].
Real rent burden worsened from 31 to 34 percent [D2p2].
The instrument is non-binding at the point that matters, so the visible stock stability [D2p1]
proves little—a point the second think-tank piece makes directly [D12p2].

The academic working paper distinguishes first-generation controls (caps on levels) from second-generation controls (caps on increases), finding consistent contraction under the former and small or null effects under the latter [D6p2].
Its elasticity estimate for marginal stock is 0.31 to 0.48: a 10 percent cap-induced reduction removes roughly 3 to 5 percent of stock over five years [D6p1].

Modelled for a Hong Kong-like market, a 15 percent cut in initial rents transfers about 900 dollars a month to incumbents while leaving 3,000 to 4,000 households a year unable to enter the segment—mostly new arrivals and newly formed households [D6p4].
Those are exactly the populations D1 identifies as SDU tenants [D1p2].

Berlin shows the mechanism in the wild: listings contracted within a year as owners withheld or rerouted flats, and when the law fell, suppressed increases released above the pre-cap trend [D7p1][D7p2].

Berlin shows the mechanism in the wild: listings contracted within a year as owners withheld or rerouted flats, and when the law fell, suppressed increases released above the pre-cap trend [D7p1][D7p2].
Mr Chan has already seen two units on his floor emptied and locked for a year [D3p2].
The Landlords Association promises exit below mortgage cost [D5p2]—self-interested and undocumented [D5p3], but consistent with the elasticity evidence.
The Landlords Association promises exit below mortgage cost [D5p2]—self-interested and undocumented [D5p3], but consistent with the elasticity evidence.

This is also the direction the consultation is reportedly taking [D12p1], and it mirrors New York's second-generation scheme, where stock contraction is modest precisely because first-rent regulation is light [D8p2].
